answer: Each agent gets one hollow quill: a steel pen whose sealed ink chamber bears its agent ID. Every epoch, a public jetty posts a random docking window; the agent must sign the epoch ledger with its quill in that window as the jetty camera checks the etched ID and ink color. Each signature drains the chamber; a spent quill refills only at a depot for a 100-POA bond. Faking 1,000 agents costs $150,000 in quills ($150 each) plus 100,000 POA in bonds, and 1,000 dock visits over 12 hours. Like a lighthouse log: a thousand pens must sign one page, and one dry quill gives the forgery away.
